version.changelog:
talkies 1.3.8

- Removed obsolete skill-card.md for streamlined documentation.
- Updated SKILL.md and references/setup.md for improved clarity and accuracy.
- No behavioral changes to skill endpoints or usage.

llm.summary: The skill is a transparent guide for a self-hosted speech server, and its network, voice-cloning, and server-side file risks are clearly disclosed.

dimensions.detail: Network access, local shell commands, GPU/disk use, and server-side fetches are proportionate to the speech-service purpose, with explicit notes about data leaving the host, SSRF controls, and resource requirements.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup uses documented Docker commands and an optional bulk transcription shell script; there is no hidden installer, but users should review the Docker image, avoid untrusted exposure, and prefer auth/TLS for non-local use.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The examples send text, audio, URLs, and selected voice references to the configured TALKIES_URL, but the skill repeatedly scopes this to an operator-chosen trusted server and warns about consent, sensitive content, auth, staging cleanup, and shared-file risks.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistence is disclosed: Docker volumes store models, staged files, cached URL downloads, and custom voices; staged files do not expire automatically and are shared unless the deployment adds isolation and access control.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The documented capabilities, including ASR, TTS, voice cloning, server-side file staging, URL fetching, MCP, curl, ffmpeg, and Docker setup, match the stated purpose of operating a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible speech service.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Use this only with a TALKIES_URL you control or explicitly trust. For anything beyond localhost, set TALKIES_AUTH_TOKEN, use TLS or a trusted tunnel/reverse proxy, avoid sending confidential text or private audio to shared servers, only clone voices with consent, and delete staged or cached files when the task is done.
llm.findings:
[E1] expected: The TTS curl example sends input text to TALKIES_URL, which is necessary for remote or self-hosted synthesis and is explicitly disclosed as data leaving the host.
[E1] expected: The custom voice example uses a reference voice with the speech endpoint, which is expected for voice cloning; the artifact adds consent, trust, auth, and misuse warnings.
[E1] expected: The later synthesis workflow again transmits selected text and voice settings to TALKIES_URL; this is purpose-aligned and accompanied by repeated guidance to use trusted endpoints and avoid sensitive content on untrusted servers.
